REPORT
Date February 1, 1935.
Subject Case against two alleged communists named Sung Ma Jun alias Sung
Tsin Sung and Mo Chung alias Mo Men Sz arrested on 30.1.35 at the
request of the Public Safety Bureau.
Made by D. C. (Special Branch). Forwarded by J.B.Coo D.I.

Sung Ma Tsu (沈華芝), alias Sung Tsin Sung (沈俊生),
in his statement admits having been a member of the Communist
Party from August 1931 until March 1934 when he was expelled on
account of laziness. He claims that he then surrendered himself
to the Public Safety Bureau and became a communist suppression
informer working under the supervision of Chang I Ming (張一鳴),
and Cheng Kuei Fu (鄭耿夫), agents of the said Bureau.
Investigation of this statement reveals that he became
known to the Public Safety Bureau in the manner stated, and was
paroled. Consequently he has been kept under surveillance
by the Public Safety Bureau who now consider his surrender to
have been insincere. It is a fact that he has failed to
furnish the Public Safety Bureau with any useful information
regarding the identity of his former associates and, in the
absence of any additional evidence, the allegation of insincerity
appears to be based on this factor.

Two books seized during a search of this man's home
are sold openly in the bookstores named in his statement, and
there is no reason to doubt the claim that he purchased them
there. Regarding the political character of these books, one
of them entitled "Collection of Tolstoi's Novels" contains a
part wherein the principles of socialism are explained non-
committally. The second book is entitled "Method of Social
Research". These books may be termed mildly pro-communistic
in character.

Against the second suspect, Mo Chung (馬駿) alias
Mo Meu Sz (馬謀如), the only evidence is the statement of the
first suspect implicating him as a former communist.

由特别分部警务处总监撰写。经 J.B.Coo 警探转呈。

宋马祖（沈華芝），别名宋俊生（沈俊生），在其供词中承认自1931年8月至1934年3月期间曾是共产党员，后因懒惰被开除。他声称随后向公安局自首，并在该局特工张一鸣（張一鳴）和郑耿夫（鄭耿夫）的监督下成为镇压共产主义的情报员。
对该供词的调查显示，他确实以所述方式被公安局知晓，并被假释。因此，他一直受到公安局的监视，该局现在认为他的自首不真诚。事实上，他未能向公安局提供有关其前同伙身份的任何有用信息，在缺乏其他证据的情况下，对其不真诚的指控似乎基于这一因素。

在此人家中搜查时查获的两本书在他供词中提到的书店公开出售，没有理由怀疑他在那里购买的说法。关于这些书的政治性质，其中一本题为《托尔斯泰小说集》，其中有一部分非承诺性地解释了社会主义原则。第二本书题为《社会研究方法》。这些书可被称为具有温和的亲共性质。

针对第二名嫌疑人莫骏（馬駿）别名莫谋如（馬謀如），唯一的证据是第一被告指认他为前共产党员的供词。

At 3:30 p.m. on 30.1.35, D.S. Sansom, Special
Branch, came to Pootoo Road Station accompanied by
Inspector Dong Pau of the Public Safety Bureau and
requested assistance to execute two S.S.D.Court warrants,
one giving authority to search the Sung Zung Shing
(沈承鑫) macaroni shop at 978 Tonquin Road and the other
to arrest one Sung Hwo Tsz (沈華芝), an employee of
the above shop.

Assistance was rendered by D.S.I.s Rhind, Chao
Ping Kun and C.D.S.113. In the course of the search,
two booklets were found lying on a bench in the shop
portion of the premises. These publications, which are
entitled respectively, "Collection of Tolstoi's Novels"
and "Method of Social Research" and are being deemed to
be of a pro-communistic character, were seized.

The man Sung Hwo Tsz was found in his bedroom
which is situated above the shop and he was accordingly
put under arrest on the authority of the second warrant.
With him at the time was one Ho Chung (馬駿) alias
Ho Mau Sz (馬茂如) who stated that he was merely on a
visit and he was brought to the station for enquiry.
His home situated at No.8 Ong Shing Li (陽慶里), Tatung
Road, Chapel, was subsequently searched but no trace of
any incriminating matter could be found.

1935年1月30日下午3时30分，特别支部副督察桑森（Sansom）在公安局董保（Dong Pau，音译）巡官的陪同下抵达普陀路捕房，请求协助执行两张特区法院令状，一张授权搜查位于通金路978号的沈承鑫面馆，另一张授权逮捕上述面馆的一名雇员沈华芝（Sung Hwo Tsz）。

林德（Rhind，音译）副督察长、赵炳坤（Chao Ping Kun，音译）副督察长及刑事侦缉警员113号提供了协助。在搜查过程中，在该处所的面馆部分的一张长凳上发现了两本小册子。这些出版物分别题为《托尔斯泰小说集》和《社会研究法》，被视为具有亲共性质，遂予扣押。

男子沈华芝在其位于面馆楼上的卧室内被发现，因此依据第二张令状将其逮捕。当时与他在一起的还有一人何骏（Ho Chung），别名马茂如（Ho Mau Sz），此人声称自己只是来访，随后被带回捕房接受查问。其后对其位于闸北大通路阳庆里8号的住所进行了搜查，但未发现任何罪证痕迹。

The man Sung Hwo Tsz in a statement taken from
him, of which a copy is attached, admits that the two book-
lets belong to him and confesses that he has been a member
of the Communist Party since 1933, having been initiated
by one Siau Woo (小英) who is at present in the custody
of the P.S.B. for being concerned in the activities of the
party. He implicates the other man Mo Meu Sz who was taken
into custody along with him, inasmuch as he states that the
latter although not at present connected with any politi-
cal party was formerly interested in communism.

A written statement has also been taken from the
man Mo Meu Sz and a copy is attached. It will be seen that
he strongly denies being in any way associated with politi-
cal movements and declares that he merely knows Sung Hwo
Tsz for reasons of friendship. In the statement he
describes himself as an apprentice employed at the Kyung
Ung Kee (金恒记) curios shop at 17. Zeu Loh Li, Rue Hue,
in French Concession, which is owned by his uncle. He adds
however, that he has only been employed only for about one week
and prior to that time, he was unemployed.

Both men are being placed under a Writ of
Detention. On their appearance before the Second Branch of
the Kiangsu High Court on 31.1.35, a remand of three days
will be applied for in order that further enquiries may
be made.

Sung Hwa Tsz
Nanking                                      D. S. Sansom.
Postoo Rd. Stn.           30/1/35.            Clerk Chiang King-yong.

My name is Sung Hwa Tsz (沈華芝), alias Sung Tsin
Sung (沈俊生), age 24, married, native of Nanking, residing
and working with my father at the Sung Zung Shing (沈承鑫)
Macaroni Shop, 978 Tonquin Road, which has been owned by my
father for about 8 years.

I came to Shanghai about 18 years ago and took up
residence with my parents at Amoy Road.    I was educated at
a private school on Amoy Road, name unknown, for about 3 years.
I had no other education.    When my father opened the macaroni
shop, he took me into his employ, and I have been with him
ever since.

The two booklets seized at my home are mine, having
been purchased by me about 9 months ago at the Ta Tung (泰東)
and World Bookstores, Foochow Road.    I have nearly finished
them but do not consider them to be of a communistic nature.

In August, 1933, one Mau Woo (小吳) (now in
custody) introduced me to the Communist Party.    He gave me
handbills to distribute, and later obtained for me the office
of Secretary of the Publication Department of the Communist Party.
I continued in this role until March, 1934 when I was dismissed
from the Communist Party because of laxity on my part.    I then
reported to the Public Safety Bureau on my past activities and
became employed by them as an informer.    Public Safety
Bureau representatives named Tsang Ih Ming (張一鳴) and
Seng Kan Fu (鄭耿夫) frequently call on me at my home to
obtain information.    They still maintain contact with me,
the last time I saw them being about 2 weeks ago.

沈华芝
南京                                      D. S. 桑森。
普陀路捕房           1935年1月30日。            书记员蒋景荣（Chiang King-yong，音译）。

我叫沈华芝，别名沈俊生（Sung Tsin Sung，音译），24岁，已婚，南京人，现与父亲居住在通金路978号沈承鑫面馆并在此工作，该面馆由我父亲拥有约8年。

我大约18年前来到上海，与父母住在爱莫尔路（Amoy Road）。我就读于爱莫尔路的一所私立学校，校名不详，就读约3年。我没有受过其他教育。当父亲开设面馆时，他雇佣了我，此后我一直跟随他工作。

在我家中被查获的两本小册子是我的，大约9个月前我在福州路的大东书局和世界书局购买。我快读完了，但不认为它们具有共产主义性质。

1933年8月，小吴（Mau Woo）（现被羁押）介绍我加入共产党。他给我传单让我分发，后来为我谋得共产党出版部秘书的职位。我担任此职直到1934年3月，当时我因工作懈怠被共产党开除。随后我向公安局报告了我过去的活动，并被他们雇佣为线人。名为张一鸣（Tsang Ih Ming）和郑耿夫（Seng Kan Fu）的公安局代表经常到我家获取情报。他们仍与我保持联系，我上次见到他们大约是两周前。

Mo Chung
Nanking XX D. S. Samson.
Foofoo Rd. Zn. 30/1/38. Clerk Chiang King-yong.

My name is Mo Chung (馬駿) alias Mo Mau as
(馬謀如), age 19, native of Nanking, at present employed
as an apprentice in the Kyung Ung Kee (金恒記) Curios Shop
at No. 17 Zeu Loh Li (首祿里), Rae Hue, Frenchtown, and
residing at No. 5 Ong Ching Li (鴻慶里) off Tatung Road,
Chapei.

I was born in Shanghai in the year of 1916. I was
then residing in an unnumbered country house at Kyen Mou Di,
Nantao. I was educated under a private tuitor until the age
of 12, when I went to study in the Hwo Ru (華安) Primary
School at No. 9 North Chengtu Road. I left that school at the
age of 16 and obtained employment as a clerk in the Dah Foong
(大豐) Iron Factory on Ferry Road (Japanese concern). I
was discharged from that factory on August 11th in 1934 when
the staff was reduced and remained unemployed until one week ago.
The proprietor of the curios shop where I am employed is my
uncle named Kyung Ung Cheng (金恒昌).

I have an elder brother named Mo Mau Xiang (馬謀祥)
who was formerly employed with the S.M.P. Police as C.R.S. 5.
He is at present serving a term of 1 year imprisonment in the
Ward Road Gaol on charges of Assault and Misappropriation.
When he was employed with the S.M.P., I lived together with him
at 4877 Yee Ching Li off Mohican Road. We removed to this
address from Nantao when I was 16 years of age.

The man who was arrested at the same time with me
is my friend whose name is Sung Hua Tao (沈華道). I have
been acquainted with him for about 4 years.

何骏
南京 XX D. S. 桑森。
福州路 Zn. 1938年1月30日。书记员蒋景荣（Chiang King-yong，音译）。

我叫何骏，别名马谋如（Mo Mau as，原文如此，应为马茂如或马谋如），19岁，南京人，现受雇为法租界霞飞路首祿里17号金恒记古玩店的学徒，居住在闸北大通路鸿庆里5号。

我于1916年出生在上海。当时我住在南市坚摩地（Kyen Mou Di，音译）的一栋无门牌号的乡间房屋里。我接受私人导师教育直到12岁，当时我去成都北路9号的华安小学读书。我16岁离开该校，并在渡轮路（日本商号）的大丰铁厂获得职员职位。1934年8月11日，因工厂裁员我被解雇，此后一直失业直到一周前。我受雇的古玩店店主是我的叔父，名叫金恒昌（Kyung Ung Cheng，音译）。

我有一个哥哥叫马谋祥（Mo Mau Xiang，音译），以前在工部局警务处担任华籍巡捕5号。他目前因袭击和挪用公款罪名在华德路监狱服刑一年。当他在工部局警务处任职时，我和他一起住在莫干山路（Mohican Road）亿庆里4877号。我16岁时我们从南市搬到此地址。

与我同时被捕的人是我的朋友，名叫沈华道（Sung Hua Tao，音译）。我认识他大约4年。

I am not a communist and have never been interested

This is a true statement.
